Because of this, I could **not** verify MoneyHelper's tenant/landlord split wording or its quote-comparison advice, and so I **cannot confirm the "both sources agree" cross-check** you asked for. Only one source is verified below.

## ✅ Aviva contents insurance page (verified, tab 2)
`aviva.co.uk/insurance/home-products/contents-insurance/` — "Aviva Signature contents insurance"

**Named coverage limits, exactly as published:**

| Cover | Published limit |
|---|---|
| Alternative accommodation | Until your home's fit to live in, **up to £100,000 for buildings insurance, and £25,000 for contents insurance** |
| Home office equipment | Equipment "you own and are responsible for" **up to £15,000** |
| Garden contents | Contents "usually kept in the open, such as garden furniture", **up to £1,500** (conditions apply) |
| Visitor belongings | Belongings of someone visiting your home, **up to £3,000** |
| Contents sum insured | **Unlimited** — "no limit to the overall amount we'll cover all your contents for" |
| Single items | Anything **worth more than £2,500** must be declared and noted on the policy |
| Legal services (optional add-on) | **Up to £100,000** in legal costs per claim |
| Home emergency (optional add-on) | **Up to £1,000** parts/materials per claim, plus hotel bill **up to £1,000** |

**Not covered:** wear and tear, theft of bicycles unless securely locked to an immovable object, motorised vehicles/aircraft/caravans/watercraft. Accidental damage and cycle cover are paid optional add-ons.

**Belongings vs building — confirmed on Aviva's page:** *"Contents insurance only covers your belongings – it doesn't give you protection for the building itself."* The page also separates the renter and landlord routes, linking "contents insurance for tenants" for renters and "home insurance for landlords" for rental properties — consistent with the structure being the landlord's responsibility. This is Aviva's wording only; the MoneyHelper corroboration is still outstanding.

## 💷 Is a price published?
**No — no premium is published anywhere on the page.** I searched the full page text: the only occurrence of "how much" is in the quote-process description ("pick how much you'd be prepared to pay towards the cost of a claim"), and there is no "from £X" teaser price. Every price route is a **live quote** ("Get a quote" / "Continue your saved quote"), and Aviva's own explainer states *"Your premium depends on factors like your risk of claiming."* A real figure therefore requires starting a quote with personal details.

As instructed, I did **not** start or submit any quote and entered no personal or payment details. Both source tabs remain open for you to verify.
